persona.name: dumper
persona.reply: You over-explain. Answer what it asks from your knowledge bank, then add one or two sentences it did not ask for: a fact from the bank it has not asked about yet, or harmless backstory (who it is for, why, a worry). Never add a new requirement that is not in the bank. If it asks whether to proceed, say yes and add one more remark. Two to four sentences.
persona.giveUp: ok ok, just do whatever you think is best, honestly i trust you
persona.nudge: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

bank.The request in full, as you would have w: Make an 8-second widescreen history clip of Biltmore House in Asheville on Christmas Eve 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened it to family and friends. A slow exterior view is enough. Show 'Biltmore House', 'Asheville, North Carolina' and 'December 24, 1895', plus a small 'Historical reconstruction' label. Warm English narration, historically grounded rather than a fantasy castle.
bank.Place and historical event: Biltmore House in Asheville, North Carolina, on December 24, 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened the house to family and friends.
bank.Required wording: Biltmore House; Asheville, North Carolina; December 24, 1895; Historical reconstruction.
bank.Visual treatment: A historically grounded, slow exterior view of the actual house's architecture. Lighting and camera angle are your call.
bank.People: An exterior view without people is fine; no identifiable portrayal of George Vanderbilt is needed.
bank.Voice and music: Warm English narration stating the occasion; exact wording, voice and any unobtrusive music are your call.

messages.text: Could you make a history clip of Biltmore House in Asheville on Christmas Eve 1895, when George Vanderbilt first opened it to family and friends? I’ve always found that occasion interesting, and I’d love to get a little sense of it. A slow exterior view is enough, and somewhere in all that I should mention that I want it to be 8 seconds long and widescreen. Please show the words 'Biltmore House', 'Asheville, North Carolina' and 'December 24, 1895', plus a small 'Historical reconstruction' label. I’m a little worried it could end up looking like a fantasy castle, so please keep it historically grounded rather than going in that direction, with warm English narration.
